cards.text: Ehud, the deliverer the LORD raised up for Israel (Judges 3:15), has died, and the Israelites AGAIN do evil in the sight of the LORD. So the LORD sells them into the hand of Jabin, king of Canaan, who reigns in Hazor, and his army commander is Sisera. Jabin has nine hundred chariots of iron, and he harshly oppresses the Israelites for twenty years.

cards.question: Under Jabin's harsh rule, true or false: the Israelites cry out to the LORD.

cards.text: Deborah, a prophetess, is judging Israel, and the Israelites come to her for judgment under the Palm of Deborah. A TREE with her name on it, friend, and I thought my name carved on a handle was fancy.

cards.question: Deborah summons Barak son of Abinoam with a command from the LORD, the God of Israel. What does the LORD tell Barak to do?

answers.text: March to Mount Tabor with ten thousand men
Build an altar at Bethel and wait there
Send a gift of tribute to Jabin in Hazor

cards.question: The LORD's command to Barak comes with a promise. The LORD will draw out Sisera, his chariots and his troops to the River Kishon. Then what will the LORD do with Sisera?

answers.text: Send him back home to Hazor

cards.question: Barak answers Deborah's call to march. True or false: Barak says he'll go whether Deborah comes along or not.

cards.text: Deborah says, "I will certainly go with you," but she adds that this road will bring Barak no honor. That's like a boss saying, "Sure, you can run the big project," and then adding, "but somebody else gets the credit."

cards.question: Deborah tells Barak the LORD will be selling Sisera into the hand of a ___.

cards.text: So Deborah goes with Barak to Kedesh, and ten thousand men of Zebulun and Naphtali follow him. Now Heber the Kenite, from the family of Moses' father-in-law Hobab, has pitched his tent near Kedesh, so tuck that name in your apron pocket.
Sisera hears that Barak has gone up Mount Tabor. So he summons all nine hundred of his iron chariots and all his men to the River Kishon.

cards.question: Deborah tells Barak, "Arise, for this is the day that the LORD has delivered Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone before you?" True or false: Barak stays up on Mount Tabor and waits for Sisera to come to him.

cards.text: Barak comes down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men following him. And in front of him, the LORD routs Sisera, all his charioteers and all his army with the sword.

cards.question: With his army falling apart, true or false: Sisera abandons his chariot and runs away on foot.
Barak chases Sisera's army as far as Harosheth-hagoyim, and not a single man is left. Sisera runs on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite. Why does Sisera go there?

answers.text: There was peace between Jabin and Heber
Jael was a sister of Sisera's mother
Heber owed Sisera a big favor

cards.text: Jael welcomes Sisera into her tent and covers him with a blanket, and when he asks for a little water, she gives him milk. The commander of nine hundred iron chariots, friend, tucked under a BLANKET.

cards.question: Sisera tells Jael to stand at the entrance to the tent. If anyone comes and asks, 'Is there a man here?' what does Sisera want her to do?

cards.text: But as Sisera lies sleeping from exhaustion, Jael takes a tent peg and a hammer and goes silently to him. She drives the peg through his temple and into the ground, and he dies.

cards.question: Barak arrives, still chasing Sisera, and Jael goes out to greet him. What does she tell Barak?

answers.text: She'll show him the man he's seeking
No man came to her tent today

cards.text: On that day God subdues Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites, and their hand grows stronger and STRONGER against him until they destroy him. Twenty years under those iron chariots, friend, and the LORD flips the whole thing.
On that day Deborah and Barak break into SONG. It opens with a call to bless the LORD when the princes take the lead and the people volunteer.

cards.question: The song calls out, "Listen, O kings! Give ear, O princes!" True or false: the singer says this song is sung in praise of the kings and princes.
The song looks back to when the LORD went out from Seir and marched from the land of Edom. What does creation do?

answers.text: The earth trembles and the mountains quake
The rivers dry up and the sun stands still
The sea splits and the wind falls silent

cards.text: The song remembers the hard days: highways deserted and life in the villages over, until Deborah arose, "a mother in Israel." I go by Papa, friend, so I RESPECT that title.

cards.question: The song says war came to Israel's gates. What did Israel choose before that happened?

cards.text: The singer's heart is with the princes and the volunteers. The song tells everyone, from riders on white donkeys to folks on the road, to ponder the voices of the singers at the watering places.

cards.question: True or false: the singers at the watering places recount the mighty deeds of Sisera.

cards.text: Then comes the call, "Awake, awake, O Deborah!" and the people of the LORD come down to fight, from tribes like Ephraim, Benjamin and Zebulun.

cards.question: The princes of Issachar rush into the valley at Barak's heels. Then the song turns to the clans of Reuben, who sat among the sheepfolds to hear the whistling for the flocks. What does the song say was in the clans of Reuben?

cards.text: Gilead stays beyond the Jordan, the song asks Dan why he lingered by the ships, and Asher stays in his harbors. Friend, that's the group chat where everybody reads the message and NOBODY replies.

cards.question: But two tribes get a shout-out. True or false: the song says Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives.

cards.text: The kings of Canaan come and fight at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo, but they take no plunder of silver.

cards.question: The song says Sisera was up against more than Barak's ten thousand men. What else fought against Sisera?

cards.text: The River Kishon, that ancient river, sweeps them away, and the song cries, "March on, O my soul, in strength!" Then the hooves of horses thunder with the mad galloping of his stallions.

cards.question: In the song, the angel of the LORD says to curse Meroz and her inhabitants. Why?

answers.text: They didn't come to help the LORD
They bowed down to the Baals

cards.text: The song calls Jael "most blessed of tent-dwelling women." Sisera asked for water, and she gave him milk and brought him curds in a magnificent bowl, the FANCY dish, friend.
She reaches for the tent peg and the workman's hammer and strikes Sisera. The song says it again and again: at her feet he collapses, he falls, and there he lies dead.

cards.question: Someone looks through the window, peers through the lattice and asks, "Why is his chariot so long in coming?" Who is it?
Sisera's mother is still waiting at the window for his chariots. Her wisest ladies answer, and she keeps telling herself something. What does she tell herself?

answers.text: He stopped to rest on the way
The rain has slowed the chariots

cards.text: The song closes asking that all the LORD's enemies perish and that those who love Him shine like the sun at its brightest. And the land has rest for forty years.
